label: Kodak Tri-X 400
source: Kodak Alaris, KODAK PROFESSIONAL TRI-X 320 and 400 Films technical data, KODAK Publication No. F-4017 (December 2016, revised 12-16); curves read from the PDF's vector chart paths (pages 7 and 8)
notes: Approximate digitization; not supplied or endorsed by Eastman Kodak Company or Kodak Alaris. All charts used are vector paths in the PDF; curve vertices were read directly from the path geometry (straight segments as given, cubic Bezier segments sampled at 16 steps; no raster tracing) and axes calibrated on the vector frame and tick marks (log H -4.0..+1.0, density 0..4.0; 250-750 nm, log sensitivity 0..4.0), the tick positions cross-checked against the printed tick labels; characteristic curves resampled linearly on a 0.02 log H grid, spectral curves on a 1 nm grid. Data are for KODAK PROFESSIONAL TRI-X 400 Film / 400TX (135 and 120). The same publication also charts TRI-X 320 Film / 320TXP sheets (page 8 HC-110 Dilution B 4/6/9/14 min, page 9 D-76); that is a different product and is not included. Characteristic curves ('Densitometry: Diffuse visual'): four 400TX charts, page 7 KODAK PROFESSIONAL T-MAX Developer small tank 20 C (68 F) 6/7/9/11 min for 35 mm and for 120-size, page 8 KODAK PROFESSIONAL D-76 Developer large tank 20 C (68 F) 6/8/10/12 min for 35 mm and for 120-size; all sixteen are in all_curves. Curves were matched to their time labels by their dash pattern against the chart legend, and the match was checked by density order at log H -1.0 (longer time, higher density). channels.k is T-MAX Developer small tank 20 C (68 F) 6 min, 35 mm: the manual-processing starting points (page 2) are 'intended to produce a contrast index of 0.56', and the 400TX table (page 3) gives T-MAX Developer small tank at 68 F (20 C) for 6 min, which is the only charted curve that equals a recommended starting-point time and temperature (the D-76 large-tank starting point at 68 F is 7 3/4 min, between the charted 6 and 8 min). 35 mm is used over 120-size as the main 400TX format; the 120 curves have a lower base-plus-fog (0.16-0.27 at log H -3.45, against 0.27-0.38 for 35 mm) and are kept in all_curves. The charts begin at about log H -3.45; nothing is charted below that. Toe vertex noise was removed with a running maximum so density is non-decreasing. x is log H (lux-seconds) as charted. log_h_ref: none. The charts carry no 18% grey, speed-point or normal-exposure mark, so no reference exposure is placed; the exposure tables give EI 400 for 400TX. Spectral sensitivity (page 7): 'LOG SENSITIVITY', sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (erg/cm2) required to produce the specified density; effective exposure 0.5 sec, diffuse visual densitometry. The chart is not labelled with a film name and the publication covers both TRI-X 320 and 400; it is used here as the published TRI-X spectral sensitivity. Two curves are charted, D = 0.3 and D = 1.0 above gross fog; channels.k is the D = 1.0 curve (mid-tone level), and both are kept in spectral_sensitivity.all_curves. As printed, the D = 0.3 (dashed) curve lies about 1.0-1.3 log units below the D = 1.0 (solid) curve; the legend assignment is kept as published. Only the curve shape matters to the model, which normalizes exposure on mid grey. The red cut-off of both curves runs down to the chart floor (log sensitivity 0.0) at about 657-670 nm; values there are clipped by the chart frame, not measured, and the model treats sensitivity beyond the last wavelength as zero. rms_granularity is the printed diffuse rms granularity 17 for TRI-X 400 ('fine'; net diffuse density 1.0, 48 um aperture, 12x; image-structure data based on development in KODAK HC-110 Developer (Dilution B), 68 F (20 C)); TRI-X 320 is 16. No granularity curve is published. Not recorded (no field in this schema): contrast-index vs development-time curves (page 8), MTF curve (page 7), filter factors, reciprocity and push-processing tables.
